items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: So Fifi, the fellow's name was Fifi somebody they called him. He was one of them socialites... So he bought out the store next door... and hired John Kirby's band to play for the people who were waiting.

ctx.x: What street? About 54th Street, on the East Side, someplace. It was a tremendous club. It was a great big beautiful room and they had a band in there. So Fifi, the fellow's name was Fifi somebody they called him. He was one of them socialites, you know, with all the Vanderbilts and the Astors and the whatchacallit used to go. Cholly Knickerbocker, that sort of thing. So he bought out the store next door and turned it into a little small nightclub for the people who were waiting, to give them someplace to wait…

band to play for the people who were waiting. And the decor was beautiful. It was like palm trees and all this, and he bought us suits, uniforms, green, beautiful, you know, white jackets. Oh, it was beautiful, real beautiful, yeah. So while we were playing there we had a nice room upstairs, you know. We could lounge around between sets. And Spencer had been to the doctor and the doctor gave -- told him to knit. Knit, you know. Knit, for therapy, I suppose. And he knitted an afghan. Oh, it must have been a huge…
